name: Cardiff University

programs.title: Business, Economics, Accounting and Finance - Accelerated
programs.summary: This pathway gives you the skills and knowledge to succeed in an undergraduate degree in the fields of accounting, banking, business management, and mathematics.

programs.title: Engineering, Physical Science and Computer Science - Accelerated
programs.summary: Once you progress from this pathway, you can choose from a range of innovative degrees in civil engineering, computing, physics and more.

programs.title: Business Management
programs.summary: Get the business skills and knowledge you need to progress to an undergraduate business degree at Cardiff.

programs.title: Computer Science and Cyber Security
programs.summary: Develop technical and analytical skills to understand computing systems, protect digital environments and prepare for a wide range of future‑focused technology careers.

programs.title: Journalism, Media and Culture
programs.summary: Explore how media, journalism and culture shape our understanding of the world through modules like Media, Culture and Society, Foundations of Journalism and Advertising and Consumer Culture.

programs.title: Psychology
programs.summary: The International Year One in Psychology expands your skills and knowledge to the level required to progress to the second year of an undergraduate degree at Cardiff University.

programs.title: Arts, Humanities, Law and Social Sciences
programs.summary: Choose this pathway to progress to degrees in subjects like English, Journalism, History, Politics and many more. There are four routes: Law, Humanities and Social Sciences, Music, and Psychology.

programs.title: Business, Economics, Accounting and Finance
programs.summary: Studying business-related subjects will give you the option to progress to a degree in subjects including accounting, business management, financial mathematics, or a dual honours degree with a humanities subject.

programs.title: Engineering, Physical Sciences and Architecture
programs.summary: Choose to progress to a degree in architecture, environmental geography or an engineering subject. Specialise in one of five routes: architecture, chemistry, computing, earth and ocean sciences or engineering, physics and mathematics.

programs.title: Health, Medical and Life Sciences
programs.summary: Start your studies and work towards a career in health sciences by selecting one of four routes leading to a range of progression degrees. The routes are: Dentistry, Medicine, Pharmacological and Life Sciences, or Psychology.

programs.title: Accounting and Finance
programs.summary: Study modules in accounting and finance alongside Academic English Skills. You can choose from undergraduate degrees that have the option of a professional placement year.

programs.title: Engineering
programs.summary: Develop your knowledge of engineering and polish your English skills. Choose from degrees including Architectural Engineering and Civil Engineering, all with the option of a year in industry.

programs.title: International Relations
programs.summary: Expand your understanding of the most important issues facing the every-changing modern world, as well as gaining valuable English language skills.

programs.title: Law
programs.summary: Build your skills and subject knowledge for the LLB Law. Gain practical experience and study areas including criminal law and public law.

programs.title: Business, Economics, Social Sciences and Humanities
programs.summary: Work towards studying your Master’s degree in a wide range of subjects including Business Management, Education, Journalism and Sustainability, Planning and Environmental Policy. There are three routes: Business Management, Social Sciences and Humanities, and Human Geography and Planning.

programs.title: Science and Computing
programs.summary: Prepare to study Computing, Computing and IT Management or Software Engineering at Master’s degree level by choosing one of two routes: Computing or Software Engineering.

description: Cardiff is a vibrant modern city with a multicultural history, just two hours by train from London. It is a small city and almost everywhere can be reached on foot from the University. It is safe and friendly, with students making up 20% of the population.
